review_candidates.title: Partnership Facilitator II
review_candidates.description: PARTNERSHIP FACILITATOR II Location: Ganze, Kilifi County, Kenya Candidates must reside in or be willing to relocate to Ganze or the surrounding Kilifi County area. Please submit your resumé in English. What is the purpose of this role? The Partnership Facilitator II (PF II) serves as Compassion’s primary liaison to local church partners and is responsible for strengthening church ownership, capacity, and resource mobilization to help churches effectively minister to children and youth within their communities. This role supports approximately 14 church partners in Ganze, Kilifi County, and works closely with pastors, church leaders, children, youth, caregivers, and Church Facing Team (CFT) members to advance sustainable ministry outcomes. Through relationship building, church maturation, facilitation, and coordination of cross-functional support, the PF II helps churches develop the capabilities and resources needed to sustain ministry impact and improve outcomes for children and youth. What will you do in this role? Maintain a personal relationship with Jesus Christ and serve as a consistent witness through Christ-centered leadership, service, and prayer support for Compassion’s ministry. Promote and uphold Compassion’s child protection standards by integrating safeguarding principles into all activities and appropriately reporting concerns related to child abuse, neglect, or exploitation. Serve as Compassion’s primary relationship manager and trusted liaison for assigned church partners, fostering relationships characterized by mutual respect, trust, service, and collaboration. Support approximately 14 church partners in Ganze, Kilifi County by strengthening church ownership, leadership capacity, ministry effectiveness, and long-term sustainability. Facilitate church maturation processes that help churches grow in ownership, capacity, resource mobilization, and ministry impact. Lead collaborative reflection and planning sessions with church leaders to improve child, youth, and church outcomes and identify opportunities for continuous improvement. Partner with pastors and church leaders to identify ministry development needs and coordinate appropriate support from Church Facing Team (CFT) members and organizational resources. Support churches in identifying, mobilizing, and maximizing local resources, community relationships, and partnerships that strengthen ministry outcomes for children and youth. Facilitate needs assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation processes that support effective Child and Youth Ministry programming. Encourage meaningful participation of children, youth, parents, caregivers, church leaders, and community stakeholders in ministry planning and implementation. Coordinate cross-functional support and develop Facilitation Work Plans tailored to the needs, priorities, and maturity level of each church partner. Promote collaboration, peer learning, and resource sharing among churches to strengthen ministry impact and community transformation. Facilitate the adoption and implementation of contextualized child protection standards and practices within partner churches. Ensure timely reporting and resolution of child protection concerns in partnership with child protection specialists and organizational leadership. Contribute to Partnership Management objectives, process improvements, church satisfaction, and organizational performance outcomes. Apply facilitation, mobilization, and relationship management expertise to identify church needs and support innovative, sustainable solutions. What are we looking for? Bachelor’s Degree in Community Development, Social Sciences, Development Studies, Theology, Education, Business Administration, or a related field. Minimum of three (3) years of relevant experience in community development, church partnership, nonprofit programming, capacity building, child-focused development, or a related field. Experience working with churches, faith-based organizations, community groups, or development-focused organizations. Strong relationship management, facilitation, coaching, and stakeholder engagement skills. Knowledge of community development, church capacity strengthening, and resource mobilization approaches. Strong planning, communication, problem-solving, and organizational skills. Demonstrated commitment to child protection and safeguarding principles. Valid standard driving license with the ability and willingness to travel regularly within the assigned area. Key Competencies Strong relationship-building, facilitation, coaching, and stakeholder engagement skills. Demonstrated ability to influence, collaborate, and build trust with church leaders and community stakeholders. Strong planning, coordination, problem-solving, and organizational skills. Ability to work effectively in a field-based environment with a high degree of autonomy. Commitment to servant leadership, cultural humility, and church empowerment. Passion for child and youth development and sustainable community transformation. Equivalent education, training, experience and/or certification may be substituted for any of the minimum qualifications listed above. What are the main work conditions for this role? Location Ganze, Kilifi County, Kenya. Incumbent must reside in or be willing to relocate to Ganze or the surrounding Kilifi County area. Work Environment Field-based role supporting church partners and community stakeholders throughout the assigned area. Primary responsibility for supporting approximately 14 church partners within the Ganze cluster. Physical Demands Sitting, standing, and/or walking for up to 8 hours per day. Travel Requirements May be required to travel up to 50% of normal schedule. Must possess a valid standard driving license and be willing to travel frequently throughout the assigned area to support church partners. Compassion International uses standardized job families and associated job descriptions. As such, not all employees will be responsible for all functions on this document. Employees may perform these and/or other similar type and level of duties depending on the work group and country to which they are assigned.

review_candidates.title: Nursery RN Nights
review_candidates.description: Join us as a Nursery Registered Nurse (RN) at Medical Center Enterprise! Unit: Nursery Shift : Full Time, Nights, 7pm-7am Student Loan Contribution : Up to $20k Other incentives include: Medical, Vision, Dental, 401k match & more available for Full and Part-Time roles Job Summary The Registered Nurse (RN) provides patient-centered care through the nursing process of assessment, diagnosis, planning, implementation, and evaluation. This role is responsible for coordinating and delivering high-quality care based on established clinical protocols and physician/provider orders. The RN collaborates with physicians, nurses, and other healthcare professionals to ensure effective patient care and desired outcomes, while maintaining a supportive and compassionate environment for patients and their families. Essential Functions Coordinates and delivers high-quality, patient-centered care in accordance with organizational policies, protocols, and the nursing process. Conducts thorough patient assessments and documents findings accurately, reporting changes in condition to the appropriate care team members. Utilizes knowledge of human growth and development to provide age-appropriate care and education. Administers prescribed medications, monitors for side effects, and documents administration in accordance with standards of practice. Assists physicians during procedures within the scope of documented competency and skill level. Collaborates with the healthcare team to develop, implement, and evaluate individualized care plans based on patient assessments and needs. Responds to medical emergencies and participates in life-saving interventions, such as CPR and code team activities, as appropriate. Advocates for the rights and needs of patients, ensuring their voices are heard and respected in care planning and delivery. Provides patient and family education on medical conditions, treatment plans, and post-discharge care, ensuring understanding and adherence to instructions. Implements and adheres to infection control protocols to prevent the spread of healthcare-associated infections. Monitors and operates medical equipment (e.g., IV pumps, monitors, ventilators) as needed for patient care and safety. Promotes patient safety by adhering to National Patient Safety Goals and maintaining a clean, safe environment for patients and staff. Participates in audits, chart reviews, and compliance checks to ensure adherence to standards of practice and regulatory requirements. Demonstrates responsible decision-making in planning, delegating, and providing care based on patient needs and organizational policies. Documents patient care and education thoroughly and promptly in the medical record. Engages in professional development to maintain clinical competency and understanding of current nursing standards and regulations. Participates in performance improvement initiatives, including data collection and process development, to enhance patient outcomes and care delivery. Obstetrics/Labor and Delivery/Post Partum/Nursery RN: Educates patients about pregnancy, provides prenatal screenings, and prepares patients for labor and delivery. Assesses and monitors the new mother's physical recovery, including vital signs, postpartum hemorrhage, and potential complications like postpartum depression. Assists with epidurals and other pain management techniques during labor. Administers pain medication, induces labor, and manages other medication needs during labor and delivery. Assists during labor and delivery, monitors fetal well-being, administers medications, and provides pain relief. Monitors mothers and newborns after delivery, assessing their well-being, and providing education on postpartum care and breastfeeding. Assesses and monitors newborn health, taking vital signs, performing routine assessments, and educating parents on newborn care. Assists with gynecological exams and procedures, and provides education on reproductive health, contraception, and prenatal care. Educates patients about family planning, fertility, pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum care. Interprets fetal heart rate patterns and assesses fetal well-being using electronic fetal monitoring. Performs other duties as assigned. Maintains regular and reliable attendance. Complies with all policies and standards. Qualifications 0-2 years of experience in a clinical nursing role or student clinical rotations in an acute care setting required Knowledge, Skills And Abilities Strong knowledge of the nursing process and clinical nursing practices. Ability to perform thorough patient assessments and communicate findings effectively. Proficient in administering medications and monitoring for side effects. Effective communication and interpersonal skills to collaborate with interdisciplinary teams. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail in documenting patient care. Knowledge of safety standards, infection control, and quality improvement initiatives. Licenses and Certifications RN - Registered Nurse - State Licensure and/or Compact State Licensure required BCLS - Basic Life Support required ACLS - Advanced Cardiac Life Support preferred PALS - Pediatric Advanced Life Support preferred NRP - Neonatal Resuscitation preferred Refer to facility or unit-specific guidelines for additional requirements.

review_candidates.title: Long-Term Care Agenda Support Consultant
review_candidates.description: We improve lives The IDB Group is a community of diverse, versatile, and passionate people who come together on a journey to improve lives in Latin America and the Caribbean. Our people find purpose and do what they love in an inclusive, collaborative, agile, and rewarding environment. About This Position We are looking for a collaborative, analytical and persistent consultant to support the operational work and the knowledge agenda of the Social Protection and Labor Markets Division in the area of long-term care. This includes supporting the implementation of project “Long-Term Care Policy Dialogue and Knowledge Generation in Collaboration with Japan in Latin America and the Caribbean”, which is funded by the Japan Trust Funds. The Social Sector (SCL) has a multidisciplinary team convinced that investing in people is the way to improve lives and overcome the challenges of development in Latin America and the Caribbean. Together with the countries of the region, the Social Sector builds public policy solutions to reduce poverty and to improve the education, work, social protection and health services that citizens receive. The Sector's work aims to promote a more productive region with equal opportunities between men and women and with greater inclusion of the most vulnerable populations. The Social Protection and Labor Markets Division (SPL) prepares and supervises operations that strive to advance the goals of poverty reduction, equal opportunities, and economic growth. The team works on safety nets and transfers, early childhood development, and aging by enhancing caregiving services, expanding the coverage of social insurance and pensions, and strengthening support systems for vulnerable populations. SPL also focuses on improving employment services and training programs, ensuring better access to decent jobs, and fostering a more dynamic and inclusive labor market. What You’ll Do Support the preparation and implementation of technical cooperation and loan projects. This includes writing terms of references, identifying consultants, reviewing project related materials, producing fact sheets, monitoring project milestones, evaluating project results, managing design, execution, and evaluation of pilots, drafting project documents. This also includes supporting the implementation of project “Long-Term Care Policy Dialogue and Knowledge Generation in Collaboration with Japan in Latin America and the Caribbean”, which is funded by the Japan Trust Funds. Support and collaborate in the conceptualization, elaboration, publication and dissemination of knowledge products. Support the organization and implementation of policy dialogue meetings, events (including those of the Long-Term Care Policy Network in Latin America and the Caribbean (RedCUIDAR+)) and webinars. Support the reporting needed for all the previous items. Support regular updates of the webpage of the Panorama of Aging and Long-Term Care. Support dialogue with the Japan Trust Funds and with Japanese experts collaborating with projects funded by these Funds. What You'll Need Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in social work, gerontology, public health, public policy, economics, international development, social policy, psychology , or other fields relevant to the responsibilities of the role. Experience: At least two (2) years of progressive professional experience in long-term care, or the equivalent of education and experience. Languages: Proficiency in English and one of the other Bank official languages (Spanish, French or Portuguese) is required. Requirements Citizenship: You are a citizen of one of our 48-member countries. Must be eligible to work in job location(s) without the need for sponsorship. Consanguinity: You have no family members (up to the fourth degree of consanguinity and second degree of affinity, including spouse) working at the IDB, IDB Invest, or IDB Lab. Type of contract and duration Local Remote Consultant Full-Time, 12 months (up to 48 months, subject to eligibility) rendered 100% remotely from place of residence of the selected candidate. Services are expected to be provided from a country where the IDB Group has offices. What We Offer The IDB group provides benefits that respond to the different needs and moments of an employee’s life. These benefits include: A competitive compensation package. Leave and vacations: 2 days per month of contract + gender-neutral parental leave. Health Insurance: The IDB Group provides a monthly allowance to supplement the purchase of health insurance. Fully remote modality. Development support: We offer learning opportunities to boost your professional profile, such as seminars, 1:1 professional counseling, and much more. Health and well-being: Access to our Health Services Center that provides preventive care and health education for employees. Our culture At the IDB, we work so everyone brings their best and authentic selves to work while finding their purpose. Our people consistently strive for excellence, and we recognize and celebrate the impact of their contributions. In our efforts to drive innovation, we intentionally include all voices, cultivate a sense of belonging and champion fairness. We welcome individuals from underrepresented groups to join us and share their unique perspectives. We ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations to participate in the job interview process. If you require an accommodation to complete this application, please email us at accommodations@iadb.org.

It oversees the enterprise Balanced Scorecard and performance management framework, leads financial feasibility assessments and business case development for special projects and strategic investments, and provides strategic oversight of special projects across commercial and technical operations. The role also drives cross-functional alignment, capital allocation, program governance, and accountability to ensure initiatives deliver their intended strategic, financial, and operational outcomes in support of MTerra Solar’s growth as a renewable energy organization. Translate corporate strategy into integrated annual operating plans, strategic initiatives, performance targets, and implementation roadmaps. Conduct strategic assessments, industry benchmarking, market analysis, and business reviews to identify growth opportunities, emerging risks, and areas requiring strategic intervention. Provide strategic insights and recommendations to the Deputy CEO and senior management to support business decisions, resource prioritization, and organizational development. Ensure alignment between corporate priorities, departmental plans, budgets, and operational execution. 2. Enterprise Performance Management and Balanced Scorecard Lead the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of the enterprise Balanced Scorecard and performance management framework. Monitor enterprise performance against approved strategic, financial, operational, project development, and execution targets. Consolidate performance results, analyze variances, identify root causes of underperformance, and recommend corrective or preventive actions. Facilitate periodic management performance reviews to assess progress, address execution gaps, and recalibrate priorities when necessary. Develop executive dashboards and management reports that provide timely, accurate, and actionable insights into organizational performance. 3. Strategic Analysis and Feasibility Assessment for Special Projects Lead strategic, commercial, financial, and operational analyses for special projects, strategic investments, and other business-critical initiatives. Evaluate project assumptions, capital requirements, projected returns, funding considerations, implementation timelines, and associated risks. Conduct scenario planning, sensitivity analysis, and risk assessments to evaluate alternative strategies and investment outcomes. Monitor the performance of approved investments against business case assumptions and evaluate the realization of intended financial and operational benefits. 4. Ensure that project results are evaluated against approved objectives, financial assumptions, and expected benefits. 5. Coordinate cross-functional planning and execution among commercial, technical, project development, finance, and corporate support teams. Facilitate program reviews and management discussions to resolve competing priorities, address delivery risks, and accelerate decision-making. Promote disciplined execution, timely escalation, and clear ownership of deliverables across strategic programs. 6. Facilitate management reviews, strategy sessions, and cross-functional discussions to drive accountability and timely resolution of critical issues. Ensure the accuracy, consistency, and timeliness of strategic and performance information used for executive decision-making. Support the preparation of Board and executive committee materials relating to corporate strategy, enterprise performance, strategic investments, and major initiatives, as required. 8. Continuous Improvement and Organizational Effectiveness Identify opportunities to improve corporate planning, performance measurement, program governance, and management reporting processes. Benchmark planning and performance management practices against relevant industry standards and leading organizations. Promote a culture of data-driven decision-making, collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement. Strengthen organizational capabilities in strategic planning, financial analysis, project governance, and performance management. review_candidates.title: Group Manager System Engineering
review_candidates.description: Group Manager, System Engineering Leading Energy Sector Organisation | Perth CBD, Western Australia Brand-new executive role | Relocation and visa sponsorship available The Organisation Our client is a highly respected organisation at the centre of Western Australia’s energy system. Its WA business plays a critical role across the energy value chain, from long-term planning and connecting new facilities through to the secure, reliable operation of the power system. Western Australia’s main grid stands alone, with no connection to the east coast, which puts WA at the forefront of the energy transition, tackling technical challenges ahead of much of the world. With a wave of new wind, solar and battery connections coming and coal retirement on the horizon, engineering underpins every decision the business makes, from what happens in the coming minutes to what the grid looks like decades from now. The Role Reporting to the Executive General Manager, you will be the senior engineer on the leadership team, working alongside fellow Group Managers responsible for planning, connections, operations and change. The leadership team will rely on you for trusted, independent engineering advice. You will lead System Engineering, a group of around 25 engineers and specialists working across three streams, each led by a manager reporting to you. The group is a shared capability serving the whole business, so a large part of the role is working with your fellow Group Managers to balance competing demands for engineering resources and agree priorities. You will be a visible voice for the organisation’s engineering view with government, industry and regulators and at industry forums. Key Responsibilities Bring the organisation’s engineering capability together as one effective group, establishing clear ways of working, governance, processes and structure. Work with fellow Group Managers to triage and prioritise competing demands for engineering support across planning, connections and operations. Lead the power system studies, grid modelling, engineering and congestion analysis that support secure, reliable operation and development of the power system. Oversee engineering assessment for facility commissioning, generator performance and event investigation, as a growing pipeline of new connection applications comes forward. Provide independent technical advice and constructive challenge to the Executive General Manager and leadership team. Establish technical governance, engineering standards and assurance so the organisation’s engineering advice is robust, consistent and able to withstand external scrutiny. Represent the organisation’s engineering view to government, network businesses, industry participants and regulators, explaining complex technical issues plainly to non-technical audiences. About You You are an experienced engineering leader with the technical depth to be the senior engineer on an executive team, and the leadership maturity to bring people together. You may currently lead system engineering, power system studies or network planning at a system operator, transmission business or utility, in Australia or internationally. You are comfortable in a matrix, where influence matters as much as authority, and you can keep business as usual moving while you build the function for the future. Experience of the WA energy sector is not essential; you will be backed by deep in-house regulatory and commercial expertise. Above all, you bring a ‘how might we solve this?’ mindset. You enjoy problems that no one has quite solved yet, and you want the agency, authority and accountability to solve them. Required Skills and Proficiencies Tertiary qualifications in engineering, ideally electrical or power systems; chartered status (CPEng or equivalent) is highly regarded. 15+ years’ experience in the energy industry, including senior leadership in a medium or large organisation. Deep power systems expertise, ideally gained in system operations, planning or transmission. Experience establishing or transforming technical functions, including operating models, governance, capability and resource planning, and ways of working. Strong matrix leadership and stakeholder skills, with the ability to influence peers and build trusted relationships with government, industry and regulators. Exceptional communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical matters plainly to non-technical audiences. The Rewards and Culture This is a rare chance to shape a brand-new function at the centre of one of the most interesting energy systems in the world. From this role you see the whole energy transition: every time horizon, from real-time operations to long-term planning, and both fossil and renewable generation. You will have real visibility and influence over all of it, within a well-established organisation with the credibility and networks to make a difference. Our client offers an attractive executive remuneration package, with relocation and visa sponsorship support for the successful candidate. The team is based in the Perth CBD, with flexible working and a genuine focus on work-life balance, alongside the lifestyle Perth is known for. You will join a collaborative leadership team that helped design the new operating model and is committed to making it work. Our client has a values-led, collaborative culture and is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive workplace for all employees. How to Apply Apply now by submitting your current CV (in Word format) via our online application process. For a confidential discussion or to review the full position description, please contact Nathan Kelly on 0418 742 529 or via nathan@talentnation.com.au. Relocation support and visa sponsorship are available for the successful candidate. Talent Nation encourages applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and people of all cultures, abilities, sexes and genders. Applicants can request a reasonable adjustment at any stage during the recruitment process. Please contact us so we can provide adjustments for you.
